artifact_seen.note: Inline text in the request (synthetic fixture); there was no URL to retrieve.

findings.quote: The explainer demonstrates deep understanding of the subject.
findings.explanation: Length and jargon read as depth. A padded explainer satisfies this wording without saying anything checkable.
findings.proposed_change: C2 depth (weight 0.25): The explainer explains at least two failure modes of decentralized oracle networks and, for each, names the mechanism that addresses it and one limitation of that mechanism.

findings.explanation: Any reference list satisfies it; nothing requires a cited source to support the claim it sits beside.
findings.proposed_change: C3 sources (weight 0.20): Every factual claim about a named protocol cites a source the evaluator can open and that states the claim; a citation that does not support its claim counts against this criterion.

items.rationale: Two of the five criteria reward the appearance of quality rather than checkable content; the other three are at least observable.

findings.quote: The content is original and not generic.
findings.explanation: Originality cannot be checked from the submission and its sources; the evaluator has no corpus to compare against.

items.rationale: Only C4 depends on something the evaluator cannot check from the submission and the sources it cites.

effort.note: Checked each criterion for what the evaluator would need in order to apply it.

items.rationale: The weights favour accuracy, which fits the purpose, but with no must-pass gate a confident, well-written explainer with a few errors can still clear 75. A gate on "contains no factual errors" would protect the purpose better than the weight does.

effort.note: Considered the weights and the stated threshold together.

limitations: Synthetic demonstration only. The artifact is a fixture written for this example.
